summary: Owner of call-status reliability and the search / statistics APIs on a NestJS microservices stack for a legal-consultation call platform.
bullets: Designed a unified call-status resolution engine mapping 20+ Exotel telephony statuses across V1/V2/V3 webhook formats into a 10-value internal enum, with direction-, duration- and database-aware resolution logic.

Identified and fixed 13 production bugs from real call data (duplicate-webhook races, V2/V3 field mismatches, business logic overwriting telephony status), eliminating false “calls auto-disconnecting” reports that had blocked the operations team.

Killed a production double-assignment race in the inbound call router with an atomic conditional UPDATE claim, a guarded assignment write and a Redis SET NX single-flight lock, verified with a harness firing 10 simultaneous claimers against real MySQL.
Built a two-stage verification pipeline (synchronous webhook + async V3 API) with defense-in-depth (cleanup cron, delayed reconciliation) so status stays accurate despite unreliable webhook delivery.
Cut SearchCalls API latency ~50% by parallelizing sequential DB and enrichment calls; built a Call-Logs Statistics API 4× faster than the previous client-side aggregation of 1,000+ records.

summary: Shipped APIs across several microservices and the first GenAI feature in the backend.
bullets: Developed 20+ REST APIs across user, lawyer-appointment, finance and doc-server microservices covering profile, scheduling and earnings flows.
Built an audio-transcription service integrating the Google Gemini 2.5 Flash API to convert call audio to text within the Node.js backend.
Configured API Gateway routing in vs-gateway with JWT auth middleware and segregated microservice routes for cleaner service boundaries.
Built an iCalendar (.ics) generation service in Python/FastAPI with S3 storage, integrated into the appointment-scheduling flow.
